claims.claim: CoreWeave identity/tradability is NASDAQ:CRWV; current issuer Q2 2026 results and August financing disclosure are primary evidence, while StockAnalysis is retained only as independent market-data lineage.
Issuer financial and financing materials are treated as one issuer-origin family for independence purposes; market-data lineage is separate and does not inflate primary-source independence.

unknowns.unknown: Backlog conversion timing depends on delivery and service availability requirements.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue backlog was about $104B, excluding more than $25B net new commitments added in early Q3; active power exceeded 1 GW with a stated path toward >8 GW by 2030.
CoreWeave secured more than $30B of debt and equity capital year-to-date after an August $2.6B loan facility, demonstrating funding access but also very high capital intensity/leverage dependence.

Sep. 17 market cap was $44.06B versus enterprise value about $90.09B; TTM revenue was $7.59B and net income negative $1.93B, making valuation and financing risk unusually sensitive to backlog conversion.

thesisQuality.basis: Exceptional contracted AI-infrastructure demand supports the thesis, while leverage, concentration and execution dependence cap conviction.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 issuer evidence shows rapid revenue/backlog expansion and continued infrastructure scaling.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Independent Sep. 17 market data shows a large enterprise value relative to current revenue and negative trailing earnings, limiting valuation margin of safety.

catalystScore.basis: Large backlog, >$25B early-Q3 commitments and active-power expansion create identifiable near- and medium-term conversion catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Demonstrated access to large-scale financing supports execution capacity, but debt-heavy capital formation warrants a conservative governance/capital-allocation assessment.

alignment2036.basis: The issuer is directly building GPU-heavy AI compute infrastructure and power capacity required for continued AI scaling.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Integrated compute infrastructure, data-center capacity and cloud service delivery allow contracted demand to leverage the same operating platform.

bottleneckControl.basis: Secured compute and power capacity provide meaningful exposure to AI infrastructure bottlenecks, but upstream GPU/power suppliers remain outside CoreWeave control.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Large backlog supports demand visibility, but financing conditions, deployment timing and utilization create material downside sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.basis: Contracted infrastructure and specialized deployment create some stickiness, while hyperscalers and competing AI clouds remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Large financing access supports procurement, but rapid expansion remains dependent on GPUs, power and data-center delivery, making resilience below average.

pricingPower.basis: Large contracted commitments indicate customers accept substantial capacity economics, but exact contract pricing and renewal economics remain opaque.

riskEvidence.basis: Very high capital intensity, debt dependence, negative trailing earnings, GPU/power supply dependence, customer concentration and backlog-conversion conditions materially elevate risk.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current issuer backlog and financing evidence plus independent market valuation support reproducible treatment; full contract economics and customer concentration remain documented non-gating unknowns.
